chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (mercy of God be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Ruyani said: 'Abd al-'Azim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Zayd ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:
regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "(Some) faces on that day shall be bright, looking to their Lord"
"(Some) faces on that day shall be bright, looking to their Lord"
meaning illuminated, awaiting the reward of their Lord.

key_terms.نَّاضِرَةٌ: Bright, shining, or radiant (describing the faces of the righteous)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Rida say about the meaning of 'faces bright, looking to their Lord' in Surah Al-Qiyamah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) elucidates the concept of *Ru'ya* (Vision) by interpreting the 'bright faces' in Surah Al-Qiyamah as a sign of spiritual illumination and eager anticipation for divine reward. This exegesis highlights the psychological and spiritual state of the righteous, linking their faces reflecting inner light as they await the beatific vision of Allah, a key theme in Shia theological discussions on the nature of the afterlife.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 19. `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqaq (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi said: `Ubad Allah ibn Musa al-Rawyani said: `Abd al-`Azim ibn `Abd Allah ibn `Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Zayd ibn al-Hasan ibn `Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS) said on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abu Mahmud: `Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) explained that the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High, "(Some) faces on that day shall be bright, looking to their Lord" (75:22-23) mean that “They will be illuminated, anxiously awaiting the reward from their Lord.”
